dimensions.label: Cold
dimensions.blurb: How cold the ground is compared with the rest of its own world (percentile).

dimensions.label: Day-night swing
dimensions.blurb: How strongly the surface heats by day and cools by night, ranked within each world.

dimensions.label: Bare & lifeless
dimensions.blurb: No plants: Moon and Mars have none, so the Earth target is NDVI 0 (absolute).

dimensions.label: Loose vs rocky ground
dimensions.blurb: Thermal inertia: fine loose soil heats and cools fast, rock and bedrock slowly (percentile).

dimensions.label: Frozen ground / ice
dimensions.blurb: Ice-favourable ground: hydrogen on Mars, cold traps on the Moon, frozen months on Earth.

dimensions.label: Sun angle
dimensions.blurb: Highest noon Sun of the year, in degrees. Set by latitude and axial tilt (absolute).

dimensions.label: Terrain relief
dimensions.blurb: Height variation over ~66 km, in metres: plains vs craters and mountains (absolute).

targets.name: Jezero Crater

cold.note: Mars' average surface temperature is set mainly by latitude, so the share of Mars colder than this site is taken as the area share closer to the poles (approximation).

swing.note: First-order energy balance: daily swing grows with sunlight (cos latitude) and shrinks with thermal inertia. Ranked over the whole TES map.

bare.note: Mars has no plants; any Earth vegetation is a difference.

inertia.note: TES night thermal inertia ranked over Mars, matched to apparent thermal inertia ranked over Earth's land. Different units, same idea: loose fines vs rock.

value.source: MGS TES night thermal inertia (Putzig & Mellon 2007)

ice.note: Odyssey neutron counts ranked over Mars (fewer epithermal neutrons = more hydrogen = more ground ice), matched to Earth's freezing index. Near the equator much of this hydrogen sits in hydrated minerals rather than ice, so the ice role there is an upper bound.

sun.note: Mars' tilt (25.2 deg) is close to Earth's (23.4 deg), so the same latitude gives a similar Sun path and seasons.

value.source: MGS MOLA MEGDR 16 ppd, std over ~66 km

relief.note: Same method as on Earth: 22 km block means, standard deviation over a ~66 km box.

targets.temps: Mars ground at low latitudes ranges roughly from −90 °C before dawn to 0–20 °C at midday (Curiosity REMS, Perseverance MEDA).

targets.name: Shackleton crater rim

cold.note: Diviner shows lunar average temperature is set mainly by latitude, so the share of the Moon colder than a site is the area share closer to the poles. Earth has nothing as cold: we match the role, not the number.

swing.note: Polar ground sees a low Sun circling the horizon: one of the smallest day-night swings on the Moon.

inertia.note: Polar sites lie outside Diviner's rock-abundance map. Lunar regolith (~50 tiu, Hayne et al. 2017) is looser than almost any Earth surface, so the target is Earth's lowest-inertia 5%.

ice.note: Within a few km of permanently shadowed cold traps where Diviner finds water ice can survive; among the most ice-favourable ~1% of the Moon. Diviner PRP: 100% of the ground within 3 km keeps ice stable within 2.87 m.

sun.note: The Sun never rises more than a few degrees here. On Earth even the poles get 23 deg: no Earth place matches this.

value.source: LRO LOLA south-polar DEM 240 m, std over ~66 km

relief.note: Same method as on Earth: 22 km block means, standard deviation over a ~66 km box.

facts.label: Latitude
facts.source: USGS Gazetteer / NASA Artemis III regions

facts.label: Ground with ice stable within 2.87 m

targets.temps: Diviner, within 3 km of the listed coordinate: annual maximum 105 K (-169 °C), annual average 51 K (-222 °C); this spot is a cold trap (never above 110 K). Region coordinates are approximate, and sunlit ridge tops nearby run warmer. No place on Earth gets this cold: the coldest ground measured on Earth is about −98 °C (175 K).
refs: Paige et al. 2010, Science 330:479 (Diviner cold traps)
Williams et al. 2019, JGR Planets 124:2505 (seasonal polar temperatures)
LRO Diviner polar resource product (Paige et al., PDS LRO-L-DLRE-5-PRP-V2.0)
